newsitem.title: UK: Common Fund turns down cocoa tree stock project.
newsitem.headline: Common Fund turns down cocoa tree stock project.

text.p: The U.N.'s Common Fund for Commodities poured cold water on the financing of the International Cocoa Organization's (ICCO) mammoth tree-stock project, delegates said.
"The Common Fund wasn't keen on taking it any further," said Tim Mordan of the UK, who also chairs the ICCO executive committee.

The sour note was reported by the ICCO executive director Edouard Kouame who was told by the Common Fund that the project, which according to initial estimates may cost some $14 million, did not fall within its mandate.

The decision was not definite, and the ICCO would continue to chase the Common Fund but individual countries were urged to reassess their priorities and streamline local costs which may lift up the provisional estimates significantly.

The U.N.'s Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) has promised some money for the project which will be carried out in the Ivory Coast, Ghana, Nigeria, Cameroon and Brazil but is awaiting the final cost structure. Individual countries will foot the rest of the bill.
But delegates were advised to seek additional money from other organisations that have allocations for projects in developing countries. One such source could be the European Union (EU).
